chunks: And with this chain of narration, I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

"When you are traveling, it does not matter to you if you delay the Dhuhr prayer until the time of Asr enters, so you pray Dhuhr and then pray Asr; and likewise Maghrib and the last one (Isha), you delay Maghrib until you pray it at the end of its time, and two rak'ahs after it, then you pray Isha."
ai.seo_question: How should a traveler combine and delay prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the specific mechanism of *Jam' al-Taqdim* (early combination) for Dhuhr and *Jam' al-Ta'khir* (late combination) for Maghrib and Isha during travel, reflecting the practical flexibility granted to travelers in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the scholarly distinction between combining prayers at the beginning of the second prayer's time versus delaying until its end, emphasizing the ease (*rukhsah*) intended by the Sharia for those on journeys.
